mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -4%) in at least 55% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 6-month moving averages signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% for two months signals a loss of monetary policy effectiveness, which erodes investor confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An above-consensus rise in RSAFS (retail sales) above its 3-month moving average by more than 2% in the absence of a concurrent rise in INDPRO signals a consumption-led demand shock that temporarily boosts corporate revenues but does not sustain earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days but reversal risk thereafter.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 3M MA by >2% AND INDPRO not > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes, or returns reverse to negative within the next 5 days in more than 70% of cases.
